claim: The existing Linux/WSL2 user service manager enforced a transient worker runtime deadline, killed a TERM-ignoring parent and its two descendants, preserved a native timeout failure, and accepted a separate fresh successful run.
limitations: Synthetic offline worker only; no Codex, Claude, broker, model, account, network, or paid-host calls.
The successful second unit was explicitly launched; this does not prove checkpoint resume, automatic retry, duplicate suppression, or preservation of unfinished application state.
CPU, memory and task cgroup values were observed while active; quota saturation, OOM behavior and production sizing were not tested.
NoNewPrivileges and cgroup supervision are not filesystem or network isolation. This same-user fixture is not an adversarial sandbox escape test.
No persistent unit, scheduler, timer or existing service configuration was changed. The synthetic failed unit was reset after evidence capture.
Linux/WSL2 host only; no native macOS, Windows, host reboot, WSL shutdown recovery or always-on remote-host acceptance.
Local process termination does not establish remote provider cancellation, stopped billing or reversal of external effects.
systemd latest upstream release is distinct from the accepted distribution build; no systemd upgrade was performed.
Hashes bind retained evidence bytes; they do not independently attest the execution.
Linux/WSL local synthetic tree, not provider cancellation or Mac hosting.
Configured resource limits were inspected, not saturation-tested.
